# Makefile for mygame — generated by Pak compiler
# Requires: libdragon toolchain (https://github.com/DragonMinded/libdragon)
# Usage:
#   make          — build mygame.z64
#   make run      — build and launch in ares emulator
#   make clean    — remove build artifacts

# BUILD_DIR has to be set BEFORE n64.mk is included: it defaults to `.` there,
# and every rule below is written in terms of it.
BUILD_DIR       = build

include $(N64_INST)/include/n64.mk

PROJECT_NAME    = mygame

# n64.mk's own names for these -- its %.z64 rule reads them.
N64_ROM_TITLE   = 'My Cool Game'
N64_ROM_SAVETYPE = 

RESOLUTION      = RESOLUTION_320x240
BIT_DEPTH       = DEPTH_16_BPP
FRAMEBUFFERS    = 3

RUNTIME_DIR     = $(shell pak --runtime-dir 2>/dev/null || echo runtime)


SRCS = main.c \
        player.c

OBJS = $(SRCS:%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)
DEPS = $(OBJS:.o=.d)

CFLAGS  += -g -O0 -Wall -Wextra
CFLAGS  += -DRESOLUTION=$(RESOLUTION) -DBIT_DEPTH=$(BIT_DEPTH)
CFLAGS  += -DFRAMEBUFFERS=$(FRAMEBUFFERS)
CFLAGS  += -I$(RUNTIME_DIR)
CFLAGS  += -I$(BUILD_DIR)
CFLAGS  += 

LDFLAGS += 

.PHONY: all clean run

all: $(PROJECT_NAME).z64

# n64.mk supplies the %.elf and %.z64 rules; these just declare what they are
# made of. Reimplementing them here is what made every generated project fail
# to link: N64_LDFLAGS holds raw linker options (--gc-sections, --wrap
# __do_global_ctors) which have to reach the linker as -Wl, and the link has
# to go through the C++ driver with -lc -mabi=o64, which is what n64.mk does.
$(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT_NAME).elf: $(OBJS)

$(PROJECT_NAME).z64: $(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT_NAME).elf

# Compile C sources
$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: %.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(N64_CFLAGS) -MMD -c $< -o $@

-include $(DEPS)

# ── Asset conversion rules ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The tool variables are n64.mk's own (N64_MKSPRITE, N64_AUDIOCONV): MKSPRITE
# and AUDIOCONV64 are defined nowhere, so these rules used to run the bare
# flags as a command. mksprite's --output takes a DIRECTORY and names the file
# after the input, so pointing it at $@ made a directory called hero.sprite
# with the sprite inside it, and mkdfs then skipped the empty tree.

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.sprite: %.png
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_MKSPRITE) --format RGBA16 --output $(dir $@) $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.wav64: %.wav
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_AUDIOCONV) -o $(dir $@) $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.xm64: %.xm
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_AUDIOCONV) -o $(dir $@) $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.ym64: %.ym
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_AUDIOCONV) -o $(dir $@) $<


run: $(PROJECT_NAME).z64
	ares --system Nintendo64 $<

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR) $(PROJECT_NAME).elf $(PROJECT_NAME).z64

=====SCENARIO=====
# Makefile for g2 — generated by Pak compiler
# Requires: libdragon toolchain (https://github.com/DragonMinded/libdragon)
# Usage:
#   make          — build g2.z64
#   make run      — build and launch in ares emulator
#   make clean    — remove build artifacts

# BUILD_DIR has to be set BEFORE n64.mk is included: it defaults to `.` there,
# and every rule below is written in terms of it.
BUILD_DIR       = build

include $(N64_INST)/include/n64.mk

PROJECT_NAME    = g2

# n64.mk's own names for these -- its %.z64 rule reads them.
N64_ROM_TITLE   = 'A Very Long Title Th'
N64_ROM_SAVETYPE = eeprom16k

RESOLUTION      = RESOLUTION_640x480
BIT_DEPTH       = DEPTH_32_BPP
FRAMEBUFFERS    = 2

RUNTIME_DIR     = $(shell pak --runtime-dir 2>/dev/null || echo runtime)

DFS_FILE        = filesystem/g2.dfs

SRCS = a.c

OBJS = $(SRCS:%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)
DEPS = $(OBJS:.o=.d)

CFLAGS  += -O2 -Wall -Wextra
CFLAGS  += -DRESOLUTION=$(RESOLUTION) -DBIT_DEPTH=$(BIT_DEPTH)
CFLAGS  += -DFRAMEBUFFERS=$(FRAMEBUFFERS)
CFLAGS  += -I$(RUNTIME_DIR)
CFLAGS  += -I$(BUILD_DIR)
CFLAGS  += 

LDFLAGS += 

.PHONY: all clean run

all: $(PROJECT_NAME).z64

# n64.mk supplies the %.elf and %.z64 rules; these just declare what they are
# made of. Reimplementing them here is what made every generated project fail
# to link: N64_LDFLAGS holds raw linker options (--gc-sections, --wrap
# __do_global_ctors) which have to reach the linker as -Wl, and the link has
# to go through the C++ driver with -lc -mabi=o64, which is what n64.mk does.
$(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT_NAME).elf: $(OBJS)

$(PROJECT_NAME).z64: $(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT_NAME).elf $(DFS_FILE)

# Compile C sources
$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: %.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(N64_CFLAGS) -MMD -c $< -o $@

-include $(DEPS)

# ── Asset conversion rules ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The tool variables are n64.mk's own (N64_MKSPRITE, N64_AUDIOCONV): MKSPRITE
# and AUDIOCONV64 are defined nowhere, so these rules used to run the bare
# flags as a command. mksprite's --output takes a DIRECTORY and names the file
# after the input, so pointing it at $@ made a directory called hero.sprite
# with the sprite inside it, and mkdfs then skipped the empty tree.

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.sprite: %.png
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_MKSPRITE) --format RGBA16 --output $(dir $@) $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.wav64: %.wav
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_AUDIOCONV) -o $(dir $@) $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.xm64: %.xm
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_AUDIOCONV) -o $(dir $@) $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.ym64: %.ym
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_AUDIOCONV) -o $(dir $@) $<
# ── Asset filesystem (DragonFS, built from the converted assets) ───────────
#
# n64.mk's %.z64 rule attaches $(filter %.dfs, $^) and nothing else, so the
# image has to BE a .dfs -- a `filesystem/<name>.pakfs` prerequisite was
# silently dropped and the ROM shipped with no assets in it at all.
_RAW_ASSETS      := $(shell find assets -type f 2>/dev/null)
_SPRITE_SRCS     := $(filter %.png,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_WAV_SRCS        := $(filter %.wav,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_XM_SRCS         := $(filter %.xm,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_YM_SRCS         := $(filter %.ym,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_T3DM_SRCS       := $(filter %.gltf %.glb,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_SPRITE_OUTS     := $(patsubst %.png,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.sprite,$(_SPRITE_SRCS))
_WAV_OUTS        := $(patsubst %.wav,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.wav64,$(_WAV_SRCS))
_XM_OUTS         := $(patsubst %.xm,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.xm64,$(_XM_SRCS))
_YM_OUTS         := $(patsubst %.ym,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.ym64,$(_YM_SRCS))
_T3DM_OUTS       := $(patsubst %.gltf,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.t3dm,$(filter %.gltf,$(_T3DM_SRCS))) \
                    $(patsubst %.glb,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.t3dm,$(filter %.glb,$(_T3DM_SRCS)))
_CONVERTED_ASSETS := $(_SPRITE_OUTS) $(_WAV_OUTS) $(_XM_OUTS) $(_YM_OUTS) $(_T3DM_OUTS)

filesystem/g2.dfs: $(_CONVERTED_ASSETS)
	@mkdir -p filesystem
	$(N64_MKDFS) $@ $(BUILD_DIR)/assets >/dev/null

run: $(PROJECT_NAME).z64
	ares --system Nintendo64 $<

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR) $(PROJECT_NAME).elf $(PROJECT_NAME).z64 filesystem/

=====SCENARIO=====
# Makefile for m3 — generated by Pak compiler
# Requires: libdragon toolchain (https://github.com/DragonMinded/libdragon)
# Usage:
#   make          — build m3.z64
#   make run      — build and launch in ares emulator
#   make clean    — remove build artifacts

# BUILD_DIR has to be set BEFORE n64.mk is included: it defaults to `.` there,
# and every rule below is written in terms of it.
BUILD_DIR       = build

include $(N64_INST)/include/n64.mk

ifndef TINY3D_INST
$(error TINY3D_INST is not set. Set it to your Tiny3D installation path.)
endif
# runtime/pak_math.h is entirely T3DVec/T3DMat wrappers, so it compiles its
# body only when Tiny3D is actually present.
TINY3D_CFLAGS  := -I$(TINY3D_INST)/include -DPAK_HAS_TINY3D=1
TINY3D_LDFLAGS := -L$(TINY3D_INST)/lib -lt3d

PROJECT_NAME    = m3

# n64.mk's own names for these -- its %.z64 rule reads them.
N64_ROM_TITLE   = "It's Mine"
N64_ROM_SAVETYPE = 

RESOLUTION      = RESOLUTION_320x240
BIT_DEPTH       = DEPTH_16_BPP
FRAMEBUFFERS    = 3

RUNTIME_DIR     = $(shell pak --runtime-dir 2>/dev/null || echo runtime)

DFS_FILE        = filesystem/m3.dfs

SRCS = x.s \
        y.c

C_SRCS  = $(filter %.c,$(SRCS))
S_SRCS  = $(filter %.s,$(SRCS))
C_OBJS  = $(C_SRCS:%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)
S_OBJS  = $(S_SRCS:%.s=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)
OBJS    = $(C_OBJS) $(S_OBJS)
DEPS    = $(C_OBJS:.o=.d)

CFLAGS  += -g -O0 -Wall -Wextra
CFLAGS  += -DRESOLUTION=$(RESOLUTION) -DBIT_DEPTH=$(BIT_DEPTH)
CFLAGS  += -DFRAMEBUFFERS=$(FRAMEBUFFERS)
CFLAGS  += -I$(RUNTIME_DIR)
CFLAGS  += -I$(BUILD_DIR)
CFLAGS  += $(TINY3D_CFLAGS)

LDFLAGS += $(TINY3D_LDFLAGS)

.PHONY: all clean run

all: $(PROJECT_NAME).z64

# n64.mk supplies the %.elf and %.z64 rules; these just declare what they are
# made of. Reimplementing them here is what made every generated project fail
# to link: N64_LDFLAGS holds raw linker options (--gc-sections, --wrap
# __do_global_ctors) which have to reach the linker as -Wl, and the link has
# to go through the C++ driver with -lc -mabi=o64, which is what n64.mk does.
$(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT_NAME).elf: $(OBJS)

$(PROJECT_NAME).z64: $(BUILD_DIR)/$(PROJECT_NAME).elf $(DFS_FILE)

# Assemble MIPS sources (.s)
$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: %.s
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(N64_CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

# Compile C sources (runtime)
$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: %.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(N64_CFLAGS) -MMD -c $< -o $@

-include $(DEPS)

# ── Asset conversion rules ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The tool variables are n64.mk's own (N64_MKSPRITE, N64_AUDIOCONV): MKSPRITE
# and AUDIOCONV64 are defined nowhere, so these rules used to run the bare
# flags as a command. mksprite's --output takes a DIRECTORY and names the file
# after the input, so pointing it at $@ made a directory called hero.sprite
# with the sprite inside it, and mkdfs then skipped the empty tree.

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.sprite: %.png
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_MKSPRITE) --format RGBA16 --output $(dir $@) $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.wav64: %.wav
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_AUDIOCONV) -o $(dir $@) $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.xm64: %.xm
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_AUDIOCONV) -o $(dir $@) $<

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.ym64: %.ym
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(N64_AUDIOCONV) -o $(dir $@) $<

T3D_GLTF_TO_3D ?= $(TINY3D_INST)/bin/gltf_to_t3d

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.t3dm: %.gltf
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(T3D_GLTF_TO_3D) "$<" $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.t3dm: %.glb
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(T3D_GLTF_TO_3D) "$<" $@
# ── Asset filesystem (DragonFS, built from the converted assets) ───────────
#
# n64.mk's %.z64 rule attaches $(filter %.dfs, $^) and nothing else, so the
# image has to BE a .dfs -- a `filesystem/<name>.pakfs` prerequisite was
# silently dropped and the ROM shipped with no assets in it at all.
_RAW_ASSETS      := $(shell find assets -type f 2>/dev/null)
_SPRITE_SRCS     := $(filter %.png,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_WAV_SRCS        := $(filter %.wav,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_XM_SRCS         := $(filter %.xm,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_YM_SRCS         := $(filter %.ym,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_T3DM_SRCS       := $(filter %.gltf %.glb,$(_RAW_ASSETS))
_SPRITE_OUTS     := $(patsubst %.png,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.sprite,$(_SPRITE_SRCS))
_WAV_OUTS        := $(patsubst %.wav,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.wav64,$(_WAV_SRCS))
_XM_OUTS         := $(patsubst %.xm,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.xm64,$(_XM_SRCS))
_YM_OUTS         := $(patsubst %.ym,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.ym64,$(_YM_SRCS))
_T3DM_OUTS       := $(patsubst %.gltf,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.t3dm,$(filter %.gltf,$(_T3DM_SRCS))) \
                    $(patsubst %.glb,$(BUILD_DIR)/%.t3dm,$(filter %.glb,$(_T3DM_SRCS)))
_CONVERTED_ASSETS := $(_SPRITE_OUTS) $(_WAV_OUTS) $(_XM_OUTS) $(_YM_OUTS) $(_T3DM_OUTS)

filesystem/m3.dfs: $(_CONVERTED_ASSETS)
	@mkdir -p filesystem
	$(N64_MKDFS) $@ $(BUILD_DIR)/assets >/dev/null

run: $(PROJECT_NAME).z64
	ares --system Nintendo64 $<

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR) $(PROJECT_NAME).elf $(PROJECT_NAME).z64 filesystem/

# Makefile for m4 — generated by Pak compiler
# Requires: libdragon toolchain (https://github.com/DragonMinded/libdragon)
# Usage:
#   make          — build m4.z64
#   make run      — build and launch in ares emulator
#   make clean    — remove build artifacts

# and every rule below is written in terms of it.

ifndef TINY3D_INST
$(error TINY3D_INST is not set. Set it to your Tiny3D installation path.)
endif

# body only when Tiny3D is actually present.

# n64.mk's own names for these -- its %.z64 rule reads them.

N64_ROM_SAVETYPE = flashram

RESOLUTION      = RESOLUTION_320x240
BIT_DEPTH       = DEPTH_16_BPP
FRAMEBUFFERS    = 3

RUNTIME_DIR     = $(shell pak --runtime-dir 2>/dev/null || echo runtime)


SRCS = scene.s

C_SRCS  = $(filter %.c,$(SRCS))
S_SRCS  = $(filter %.s,$(SRCS))
C_OBJS  = $(C_SRCS:%.c=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)
S_OBJS  = $(S_SRCS:%.s=$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o)
